english: Let $A=(0,0)$, $B=(6,0)$ and $C=(2,0)$, and let $D\neq C$ be the point on the line $AB$ such that $\dfrac{DA}{DB}=\dfrac{CA}{CB}$. Let $P=(0,3)$ and $Q=(2,4)$. Three of the six points $A,B,C,D,P,Q$ are chosen at random. Then the probability that the three chosen points are the vertices of a triangle is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=(0,0)$, $B=(6,0)$ तथा $C=(2,0)$ हैं, और माना कि $D\neq C$ रेखा $AB$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिसके लिए $\dfrac{DA}{DB}=\dfrac{CA}{CB}$ है। माना कि $P=(0,3)$ तथा $Q=(2,4)$ हैं। छः बिन्दुओं $A,B,C,D,P,Q$ में से तीन बिन्दु यादृच्छया चुने जाते हैं। तब चुने गए तीनों बिन्दुओं के एक त्रिभुज के शीर्ष होने की प्रायिकता ______ है।
solution: $C$ divides $AB$ internally in $CA:CB=2:4=1:2$; $D$ divides it externally in $1:2$ (harmonic conjugate): $D=\dfrac{1\cdot(6,0)-2\cdot(0,0)}{1-2}=(-6,0)$
Slopes $DP=\dfrac{3}{6}=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $DQ=\dfrac{4}{8}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow D,P,Q$ collinear; no other triple is
solution_full: By the distance formula, $CA=2$ and $CB=4$, so $C$ divides $AB$ internally in the ratio $1:2$. A point $D=(x,0)$ of line $AB$ with $\dfrac{DA}{DB}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ satisfies $2|x|=|x-6|$, i.e. $x=2$ (the point $C$) or $x=-6$.

So $D=(-6,0)$, the point dividing $AB$ externally in the ratio $1:2$ (section formula: $\dfrac{1\cdot(6,0)-2\cdot(0,0)}{1-2}=(-6,0)$); $D$ is the harmonic conjugate of $C$ with respect to $A$ and $B$.
Three points are vertices of a triangle unless they are collinear. Total choices: $\binom{6}{3}=20$.
$A,B,C,D$ all lie on the $x$-axis: $\binom{4}{3}=4$ collinear triples.

$P$ and $Q$ are not on the $x$-axis, so a triple containing one of them and two axis points is never collinear. Triples with both $P$ and $Q$: the line $PQ$ has slope $\dfrac{4-3}{2-0}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and equation $y=\dfrac{x}{2}+3$, which meets the $x$-axis at $(-6,0)=D$ only. So $D,P,Q$ is the only such collinear triple.
originality_note: New: a point set in which one point is defined as a harmonic conjugate, and the triangle count depends on noticing that this conjugate lies on the line through two other given points (way 5: section formula and counting triangles linked). Closest known: 'm points on one line and n on another: number of triangles'. Different because: a hidden collinearity must be detected by locating D first.

concept_use.Number of straight lines, triangles and: Triangles = C(6,3) minus collinear triples; the four axis points and the line through D, P, Q give 5 collinear triples.
concept_use.Distance formula, Section formula, harmo: D is located by the distance condition DA/DB = CA/CB and the external section formula; it is the harmonic conjugate of C with respect to A, B, and it lies on line PQ.
